title: Why you can't tickle yourself 🪶
subject: brain
description:
Are you the most ticklish person you know? 👇

Why can't you tickle yourself? Your brain predicts your own touch and turns it down, and a 1999 robot experiment found a way around it.

Sources: Blakemore, Wolpert & Frith, Nature Neuroscience (1998) "Central cancellation of self-produced tickle sensation", Blakemore, Frith & Wolpert, Journal of Cognitive Neuroscience (1999) "Spatio-temporal prediction modulates the perception of self-produced stimuli", UCL News ("Why can't I tickle myself?")

scenes.text: Try to tickle yourself. Nothing happens.
Every time you move, your cerebellum predicts exactly what you'll feel.
So it turns the feeling down before it even arrives.
But here's the strange part. In a 1999 study at UCL, people tickled themselves through a robot.
When the robot added a delay of just 200 milliseconds, it suddenly felt much more ticklish.
